CYBERCAB WILL CHANGE THE GAME
No steering wheel.

Just affordable, autonomous transport at scale.
Cybercab isn’t another EV.

When the cost per mile drops low enough, owning a car stops being the default.
That’s the real shift.

.@Elonmusk HAS BEEN OPEN-SOURCING FOR YEARS

Most companies build closed systems and ask for trust.

Elon has consistently done the opposite:
• Tesla open-sourced its patents so the entire industry could move faster on electric vehicles
• Tesla opened the NACS charging standard, which is now becoming the industry norm
• He open-sourced the X recommendation algorithm
• xAI open-sourced Grok Build
• And the pattern continues
While others protect their black boxes, Elon keeps opening the box.
This isn’t a recent PR move. It’s been a core approach for over a decade.
Real progress compounds faster when the best ideas aren’t locked behind walls.
Open source isn’t just a philosophy for him — it’s a strategy.

WHY THE STARSHIP CATCH CHANGES EVERYTHING

Catching the Super Heavy booster with the tower arms isn’t just a flex — it’s the key that unlocks true rapid reusability.

Here’s why it matters:
• Turnaround speed
Ocean or droneship landings still require recovery ships, transport, and heavy refurbishment. Catching the booster directly at the launch tower means it can potentially be restacked and flown again in hours or days instead of weeks.
• Cost
The rocket itself is the most expensive part of spaceflight. Rapid reuse with minimal work is what drives cost per kilogram toward Starship’s target of under $100/kg.
• Flight cadence
A multiplanetary future requires flying often. High cadence only becomes realistic when the booster can be caught and turned around quickly.
• Closing the loop
Falcon 9 proved reuse works. Starship aims for both stages to be fully and rapidly reusable. The tower catch is the biggest remaining milestone for the first stage.
This is the difference between a reusable rocket and a rapidly reusable rocket.
Everything else — Mars, the Moon, orbital industry — gets much closer once you can catch the booster and fly it again fast.
The catch isn’t the end goal.

Tesla Bloomington Megacharger (world’s first full-scale public one for the Semi)Location: 18434 Valley Blvd, Bloomington, CA 92316 (San Bernardino County, ~1 hour east of LA, near key freight routes from the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach).  

Opened: ~July 17, 2026.  

Specs: 6 dedicated drive-thru stalls, each rated up to 1.2 MW (1,200 kW). Uses the Megacharger 2 (MC2) connector (MCS-compatible).  

Access: Open to all Tesla Semi customers. Large concrete lot designed for Class 8 trucks, with charging cabinets, light poles, and pull-through bays.

It’s Tesla’s first proper public Megacharger hub (replacing/superseding the earlier smaller Ontario test site). A Semi can add hundreds of miles of range in roughly 30 minutes here.
